title: Short-term rental by-law deferred for workshop
subtitle: Industrial zone uses, Fergus downtown lighting grants, theatre and culture plans, healthcare housing, storage agreements, additional residential units.
overview: Council did not adopt the draft short-term rental licensing by-law. Council received the staff report and deferred the matter so staff can schedule a Committee of the Whole workshop to develop by-law options before year end {{vote:m4}}. Two delegates spoke on the draft: one opposed it as too heavy-handed, and one supported moderate regulation. Short-term rentals can continue as they are in the meantime.

Council also expanded the M2 industrial zone to allow all uses permitted in the M1 zone, which staff said includes medical clinics {{vote:m10}}. It activated a Fergus downtown lighting grant stream and asked staff to widen its boundary in phase two {{vote:m6}}. It moved healthcare professional accommodation from the Gartshore Street farmhouse to Craighead Cottage because Operations Centre construction is coming {{vote:m9}}.

Council adopted the Fergus Grand Theatre operations report and the Culture Action Plan. It approved a user group storage agreement template and two rezonings on the consent agenda. Earlier, a public meeting on additional residential units was held with no delegations. Council also met in closed session, and the mayor said nothing would be reported from it.

decisions.detail: Council gave three readings to a by-law adding all uses permitted in the M1 zone to the M2 zone.
Council activated the Fergus Downtown Illumination stream of the Community Improvement Plan and directed staff to extend the program boundary in phase two as staff determine.
Council approved moving healthcare professional accommodation from 965 Gartshore Street to 495 Union Street West, Fergus.
Council approved a storage agreement template and delegated signing authority to the Managing Director of Community Services or their designate.
Council adopted the Operations and Community Impact Report and directed staff to carry out its action items.
Council adopted the Culture Action Plan and directed staff to implement its action items.
Council approved rezoning applications RZ008/24 (7120 Sixth Line) and RZ009/24 (8141 Sideroad 20) in West Garafraxa, with by-laws given three readings.

debate: A delegate who operates a rental supported licensing but called the draft too extreme. Concerns were inspection and septic requirements, floor-plan disclosure, and the range of fines. The delegate suggested simple registration with insurance, a local contact and noise rules, and said fees should fund infrastructure rather than new staff.

Another delegate supported moderate regulation aimed at problem rentals rather than all operators. This delegate said rental income helps owners stay in the community and asked that tourism revenue go back to community programs.

Councillors raised long-term housing, citing a low rental vacancy rate and survey concerns. Options discussed were owner-occupied-only rules for new rentals, grandfathering existing ones, and a cap. Councillors also questioned the historic-area exemption from the 100-metre separation and how the eight-guest limit applies to additional residential units.

Councillors discussed enforcement after hours, parking, and whether demerit points and fines are enough of a deterrent. Staff said licensing should cover costs rather than raise revenue. Staff also said the draft was built on a different foundation than council wanted and proposed starting from general provisions and building the by-law with council.

On the downtown lighting grant, one councillor asked that stores outside the first phase area not be left out, which led to the boundary-extension wording. Staff said phase two had to work within the funder's tourism focus.
